invariants.description: the Hill pump: j_PMCA = -j_max_PMCA Cai^n/(K^n + Cai^n) (relative 1e-12)
the maximal rate j_max_PMCA = A_mem rho_PMCA r_PMCA / N_A (mol/s; N_A = 6.02214076e23 /mol; relative 1e-12)
the sign: the pump only extrudes Ca, -j_max_PMCA <= j_PMCA <= 0 (negative = out of the cell)
half-maximal at K: at the run point Cai = K_PMCA (0.3788 uM), j_PMCA = -j_max_PMCA/2 (relative 1e-12)

bc_sweep.rationale: Cai from 0 through rest (0.1 uM) and K (0.3788 uM) to 10 uM (a large load); the Hill coefficient over 1-4 (one to four cooperative Ca sites; Colegrove's 1.8 in the middle); the other constants by factors 0.5-2. Bounds: concentrations, densities, turnover and area non-negative, K positive (K^n divides), n within 0.5-6.

baseline.reason: an algebraic pump law; its size (rho_PMCA) is calibrated in instance wanaverbecq2003_scg and its form checked by the invariants.

calibrate.note: not_applicable here: rho_PMCA is calibrated in instance wanaverbecq2003_scg (wanaverbecq2003plasma) and the default uses its calibrated value.

parameters: wanaverbecq2003plasma: the tonic (La3+-sensitive) Ca entry that holds resting Ca; a nuisance parameter, fitted with rho_PMCA so that rest is 102 nM (start value: j_max f(102 nM) at j_max 100 amol/s)
the brief Ca load: zero except in the load sub-experiments (obs_data protocol_info)
wanaverbecq2003plasma: thapsigargin (SERCA block) has no effect on small transients, so the recovery data are those of the PMCA alone: SERCA off
with SERCA off, the pre-ER leak off too, so the ER is isolated (no slow Ca source from ER depletion)

calibrate.source: Wanaverbecq, Marsh, Al-Qatari & Brown 2003, J Physiol 550:83 (rat SCG, indo-1, 33 degC): resting [Ca2+]i 102 +- 4 nM (Results) and the recovery tau of small loads, ~5 s at 100 nM and ~2.5 s at 500 nM (Fig. 1C); values from the full text, figure not screenshotted (no PDF on disk)
